newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - May 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - May 14.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Wednesday:
* Stocks fell on concerns the Federal Reserve might increase interest rates.
* Novartis AG acquired Merck & Co Inc's crop protection business for $910 million.
* Harcourt General Inc reached a definitive agreement to acquire National Education Corp for $21 a share, or about $800 million.
* Procter & Gamble Co signed a 10-year agreement with Regeneron Pharmaceuticals Inc to develop and market new drugs.
* Southern Co formed a consortium with two leading German utilities, PreussenElektra and Bayernwer, to buy a controlling interest in Berlin electric utility, Berliner Kraft und Licht AG.
* An alliance among United Airlines, Deutsche Lufthansa AG, Air Canada, Thai Airways International Ltd and Scandinavian Airlines System was expected to outline their plan on Wednesday.
* The A.R. Baron securities firm and 13 former employees were indicted on charges they lied to investors to induce them to buy certain securities.
* Nomura Securities Co Ltd and three executives were charged by Japanese regulators with illegally compensating a client for trading losses.
* Coca-Cola Co unveiled a new advertising slogan for its Diet Coke: "You are what you drink."
* A presidential advisory commission heard conflicting testimony about whether more government regulation was needed to protect the rights of health-care consumers.
* The owner of the Los Angeles Dodgers said he has sought permission to pursue negotiations with News Corp Ltd to buy the storied baseball team.

* Nearly 10 years after International Business Machines Corp reached it first record high stock price of $175.875, the giant technology company bested that mark, closing at $177.125. But now the former No. 1 company in the U.S. is No. 9 among American companies and just No. 3 among technology firms.
* Consumers have cut back on shopping, leading to a drop of 0.3 percent in retail sales last month.
* Digital Equipment Corp sued Intel Corp accusing the company of stealing some of its patented chip designs to create Pentium microprocessors.

* Nordstrom Inc is long noted for its customer service bringing a hometown feel. But critics say Nordstrom is losing an edge to competitors who are quicker to stock shelves with the latest popular merchandise.
